observations: The flood is the metronome: wet clusters are never more than 2 crates, so one low-water window buys one cluster; dry crates are free.
Refuges carry rewards: the Aku crate stands on a steel block, a 1UP floats above a steel stack, a W[1] waits past a later refuge.
TNT appears as footing (stepping stones in water) and as a count trap, never as a path blocker.
Nitros form walls in the water and partner with enemies (column, diagonal line with a mummy, pair beside a shield researcher).
The death route holds no collectible crates, only 10 Nitros that still count via the main-route green !: the all-box goal never forces the hard route.
Checkpoint spacing: short teaching section (8), bonus-heavy C2 (44), close C3 (52), then the longest and densest section without a checkpoint.
The bonus holds 25 of 88 boxes and teaches two outline uses: footing bridge (switch 1) and explosive lid (switch 2).
Time-trial masks freeze the hazard: invincibility stops the water rising (TT fr. 24).
The level is built for two passes: the crystal without the bazooka, the skull course easy with it.

geometryObservations: **The water is the level's metronome and its gap.** Each channel is a lethal gap one low-water window long; the cycle is fixed from the start (TT intro, TA1), so the whole route is one rhythm.

**A living gauge.** The scarab crawls at low water and flies when it rises (F3 p067) and stands at the start and beside the key channels: the telegraph is an enemy you can read before you are in danger.

**Channel → stairs → dry landing.** Walled channels about 3–4 u wide alternate with three-step stairs (TT 06) and dry landings; crates on dry ground cost no window, wet crates cost one. With no side falls, everything is vertical timing.

**Three kinds of safe island:** floating red discs that ride the water (callout 2), steel blocks and stacks (callout 3), and blocks the player builds with a ! (callout 5; skull callout A). Rewards sit on them: Aku on the block, a 1UP over the stack, a crate just past the switch-built refuge.
**Switch-built refuges scale the difficulty.** In S3 the ! is optional (TA5 skips it for time); on the skull course the switches must be pressed in order to build the safe zones ahead (callout A).

**Coupled clocks.** The sliding wall footholds run their own cycle and are usable only in some water phases (P3 s95: move when the water starts receding and sits at the top edge of the block); the guide's lane (left wall, callout C; right wall in TT 21–23) turns the double timing into a line choice.

**The shield researcher is a gatekeeper with a knock-back.** Slide only; an upper-body hit throws Crash back toward the camera and he side-steps to block (F3 p067). He is taught alone at the top of dry stairs, then placed beyond a hole (callout 4) and beside Nitros (callout 7), where the knock-back or his charge is the real danger.

**The spiked mummy is a jump-only hurdle** (spiked lower body): double-jump onto its head or fake it out (P3 s88). It is met alone on dry ground first, later patrols a Nitro line, and on the skull course should simply be ignored (callout B).
**Few true gaps.** One hole guarded by a researcher (S2), one hole at the S4 bend (TT 30) and the holes under the skull footholds (callout C); everything else is water, which kills only at its peak.

**Explosives shape standing room in the water:** TNT stepping stones (S1), a Nitro column (S2), a Nitro pair beside the researcher and a diagonal Nitro fence with a mummy (S4), and skull groups with gaps at both walls (callout D).

**Escalation:** S1 teaches (one disc, two TNT steps, each enemy alone), S2 adds refuges and the guarded hole, S3 adds built blocks and sliding footholds, S4 is the longest flood with discs and no checkpoint after C3, and the skull course combines everything with no deaths allowed.

**Patience is the skill.** Callout 8 ("don't force it") and the TT intro ("accuracy over speed") say the same thing: the level punishes impatience more than imprecision, because waiting on dry ground is always possible.
**The hazard has a reward-based off switch.** Three masks give invincibility timed for the lowest water, and while invincible the water does not rise (TT 24).
**Bonus without water:** an outline bridge from a high ! (crouch high jump), floating crates used as stepping stones that vanish when broken, and an explosive lid over the rewards.
geometryTransfer: **A global flood with phasepads.** Model a flood channel as a 3.5–4.6 m (3–4 u) wide walled `pit` floored with `phasepad`s on one global cycle (solid = low water), 7–9 m long, with three-step dry stairs (≈1.7 m rise) between channels; put a visible gauge (a slow `hopper` or a bobbing marker) at each channel head.
**Islands every window.** Inside each channel place one unbreakable island (a 1.15–2.3 m steel block or a floating pad) so a window can be split in two halves; put the Aku or life crate on top of it.

**Gatekeeper beyond a hole.** A `charger` (frontal attacks fail, telegraphed dash) on the far side of a 1.2–2.3 m hole: approaching high gets you knocked back into the hole; the counter is a short hop then a slide or ram.

**Coupled-timer footholds.** A 5–7 m deep gap crossed on three `mover` blocks sliding out of one wall on their own cycle, usable only when the global cycle is in its safe phase; keep one wall-hugging line where the timing is forgiving (the left-wall rule of callout C).

**Explosive fence with a guard.** A diagonal line of four Nitros across a channel with a patrolling `spiker` (no stomp — it must be jumped), and on the optional hard line a five-Nitro quincunx with 1.2 m gaps along both walls.

**TNT stepping stones in a timed channel.** Two TNTs 2.3 m apart in a 5.8–6.9 m channel: a double jump (+1.74 m) from a TNT top reaches the far stairs, so the chain works even in the unsafe phase, while the safe line waits for the window.
